title: Simulation manifest, version 1 (draft 3)
description: A list of entities, each a bag of named components, with an envelope that says what version, vocabulary and program it came from and, once resolved, what it rests on. RFC 0001 (/docs/rfc/0001-manifest) is the normative text. Part I of the RFC is the envelope and the entity rule; Part II is the components named under $defs/components.

manifest.description: The version of this standard the document is written against. Readers reject a version they do not know.

vocabulary.description: The shared vocabulary (kind, topic, field, ledger and unit names) the components are named in; a name or a URL. Absent means the implementation's own.

include.description: Other manifests folded in first, in order, by path relative to this document or by URL; a later entity with an earlier id replaces it component by component. Absent from a resolved manifest.

entities.description: In order: the order is the layout of the result and must not affect it.

kinds.description: Resolved form only: the description of every kind the manifest instantiates, keyed by kind name, so that a reader without the implementation can check the wiring.

locks.description: Resolved form only: every record the run read, keyed by asset id, with its content hash.

id.description: An entity id: lower case, a letter first; unique in the document after resolution.

kindName.description: A kind name: family and kind, dotted, lower case.

date.description: A UTC instant: a calendar date read as midnight UTC, or an RFC 3339 date-time with a Z offset.

duration.description: A fixed length of time: an integer and a unit of seconds, minutes, hours or days. Months and years are calendar, not durations.

value.description: A parameter value: a number, a string (which is an expression where the describe types the parameter expr), a boolean, or an array of one of those.

additionalProperties.description: Any other component: carried by every reader, reported by the checker as 'no system observes it'. Never a function, never evaluated.

entity.description: A bag of components under an id. Presence is type: an entity with a kind is a module instance, with run the run, with variant a variant.

seed.description: The only source of randomness; each module's stream derives from it and the module's id.

run.description: The run window, seed and cadences; one per manifest.

place.description: A window on the WGS 84 graticule and a resolution, stated once and copied at resolution into the params of every module entity that does not set the same key. Any further key is copied the same way. At most one.

params.description: Only parameters the kind's describe lists, in the kind's units. A string is an expression where the describe types the parameter expr.

ref.description: Where the kind's implementation comes from when the engine lacks it, locked by content hash.

scores.description: Pairs of series names, simulated then observed.

shock_topics.description: Topics, or prefixes ending in a dot, whose events count as shocks.

audit.description: Advisory to the auditor; never affects the run. At most one.

set.description: Overrides: run.<field> or <id>.<parameter>. A variant may not add an entity or change a kind.

range.description: Keys ranged over instead of set: the variant is then a family of runs, one per combination. The one loop in the transport.
A uniform range or an explicit list.

language.description: The hermetic authoring language that generated this document, e.g. javascript, starlark, jsonnet.

sources.description: Every other file the program read, by name, with its hash. A hermetic program reads nothing else.

from.description: Resolved form only: the program this document was generated from, so that anyone with the interpreter regenerates it and checks the id.

type.description: expr: the value is an expression string in the run-time expression language, over the names in vars.

vars.description: For type expr: the names in scope.

on.description: A topic: the read happens when this event arrives rather than on the module's own tick.
